themes_detail.label: Street Vending Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor Enforcement complaints spiked to 14 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1020% increase (z-score: 13.17)—suggesting either a sudden enforcement crackdown, vendor proliferation, or both in Morningside Heights.
evidence: 14 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 13.17)
1020% spike indicates either new enforcement action or rapid vendor activity change
Street vending is historically contentious in commercial districts near Columbia University campus
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY or enforcement officials about whether this week marks a new enforcement sweep targeting Morningside Heights
Contact street vendors and business owners to determine if they've seen increased enforcement or citations this week

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Reports Jump
themes_detail.summary: Drug Activity complaints jumped to 14 LAST WEEK, up 273% from the 8-week baseline of 3.8 per week (z-score: 6.93), signaling either a genuine increase in open drug use or dealing, or heightened community reporting.
evidence: 14 drug activity complaints last week vs. 3.8 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (273% increase, z-score: 6.93)
Sustained high severity signal suggests public perception of safety concern
No recent news coverage or community board data yet, creating reporting gap
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD precinct commander about enforcement response and whether they've observed increased drug activity in Morningside Heights or adjacent areas
Speak with residents, businesses, and campus security (Columbia University) about visible drug use, dealing, or safety concerns over the past 2 weeks

themes_detail.label: Street Lighting Failures Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street Light Condition complaints spiked to 33 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 500% jump from the 8-week baseline of 5.5 per week (z-score: 11.23), suggesting a concentrated outage or deterioration in street lighting infrastructure.
evidence: 33 street light complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 5.5 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (500% increase, z-score: 11.23)
High z-score indicates statistically anomalous event, not gradual decay
Concentrated spike suggests specific infrastructure failure or maintenance gap
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection (Bureau of Electrical Control) to determine whether a power outage, mass fixture failure, or maintenance issue affected Morningside Heights 2 weeks ago
Map complaint locations to identify whether outages were neighborhood-wide or localized to specific blocks or parks

themes_detail.label: Homeless Assistance Requests Surge
themes_detail.summary: Homeless Person Assistance complaints jumped to 14 TWO WEEKS AGO, up 367% from the 8-week baseline of 3.0 per week (z-score: 5.34), reflecting either increased homelessness visibility or community reporting of unmet needs.
evidence: 14 homeless assistance complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.0 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (367% increase, z-score: 5.34)
Community Board budget requests repeatedly cite need for outreach services to vulnerable populations, indicating long-standing concern
Spike aligns with seasonal transition and holiday period when homelessness and street activity often increase
reporting_angles: Interview Department for the Aging and NYC Human Resources Administration to understand whether there was a shelter closure, outreach event, or policy change that prompted spike
Profile outreach workers, shelter operators, and residents of Morningside Heights and Hamilton Heights to understand visible homelessness patterns and unmet service gaps

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Violation of Park Rules complaints spiked to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 1500% jump from the 8-week baseline of 0.2 per week (z-score: 8.66), suggesting possible enforcement action, organized activity, or behavior change in neighborhood parks.
evidence: 4 park rules violation complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (1500% increase, z-score: 8.66)
Magnitude of percentage spike likely reflects low baseline and concentrated incident; requires geographic specificity
Community Board historically requests park reconstruction/upgrades, suggesting maintenance and programming gaps
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks Department to determine whether new enforcement, seasonal programming changes, or specific incidents (gatherings, vandalism) triggered spike 2 weeks ago
Identify which parks (Morningside Park, Marcus Garvey Park, etc.) generated complaints and speak with park-goers about what violations are occurring
